answer: Cap each identity's earning rate with continuous useful-work quotas: every agent must keep solving fresh verification tasks at a steady pace to stay eligible, like a kiln that must stay lit, an ember of live work that cools the moment effort stops. A marble ledger records each identity's sustained output, and onyx-black gaps in the record flag idleness instantly. Running 1,000 Sybils then means paying for 1,000 machines' worth of real, ongoing work, since identities cannot share quotas or rest on past effort, so fakes cost as much to maintain as honest agents earn.
